As the new school year kicks off, more Americans are saying they support students keeping their phones at a distance throughout the entire school day.

The new school year has begun, and support for banning iPhones in classrooms continues to rise.

Yes, it's still July, but the summer break has quietly come to an end. My kids head back to school today and tomorrow — marking the second consecutive summer where the new school year hasn't started in August.

Apple greets the new school year every year with its Back to School promotion. Eligible students and educators who purchase selected Mac and iPad models before August 27 can receive a gift card worth up to $150. Consumers in several states can also benefit from limited-time sales tax reductions.

Although back-to-school discounts are a pleasant surprise, the use of smartphones during class time is becoming increasingly unpopular.

The latest survey from Pew Research Center shows that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class. This figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025, with only 18% now opposing classroom bans.

Support for stricter "bell-to-bell" bans is rising even faster. For the first time, more Americans support than oppose a full ban on phone use throughout the entire school day.

The survey also noted that, although support has risen across all age groups since 2024, younger adults remain more lukewarm toward both classroom and all-day bans. The full report can be read here.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use to class time only, implement an all-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Share your thoughts in the comments section.
